advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the `mutmut run` invocation in `_diagnose_non_killed` (scripts/mutation_gate.py:666) with `mutation_sandbox.wrap` (and `sandbox_env`) as execute_shard does, since it also executes mutated shard code.
evidence:
scripts/mutation_gate.py:665-669: `_run(
        (sys.executable, "-m", "mutmut", "run", *mutants, "--max-children", "1"),
        cwd=root,
        env=env,
    )`

execute_shard wraps its two subprocesses (scripts/mutation_gate.py:607 `mutation_sandbox.wrap(...)`), but `_diagnose_non_killed` at line 664 builds a plain `_command_env(root)` and passes the argv to `_run` with no `mutation_sandbox.wrap`.
`mutmut run` executes the MUTATED code — this is the precise path the 2026-08-26 `rm -rf /*` incident took, per the commit message and ticket description ('this is the causal path').
The commit message claims 'Wraps BOTH shard-test-executing subprocesses' but a third subprocess executing mutant code remains unwrapped.
advisory.finding: `_diagnose_non_killed` re-runs mutants via `mutmut run` (executing mutated shard code — the exact hazard this change guards against) but the invocation is NOT sandbox-wrapped, unlike the two calls in execute_shard.
scenarios: Head run leaves non-killed mutants, triggering the diagnostic re-run, and one of those mutants reaches a destructive code path — it executes unsandboxed.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_diagnose_non_killed`, build the sandbox allow-list and env the same way execute_shard does, and wrap the line-666 `mutmut run` argv with `mutation_sandbox.wrap(...)`; add a call-site-binding test mirroring `test_the_mutmut_run_subprocess_is_sandbox_wrapped` for this function.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a call-site-binding test that asserts every `mutmut run` invocation in mutation_gate.py (not only in execute_shard) is sandbox-wrapped.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py: `_execute_shard_run_calls()` parses only the `execute_shard` FunctionDef (`n.name == "execute_shard"`), so no test asserts anything about `_diagnose_non_killed`.

The author's own comment (ticket comment) notes 'Removing the sandbox wrap from the `mutmut run` call -> all 42 tests stayed GREEN' — the same invisibility applies to the unwrapped diagnostic call, which no test covers.
advisory.finding: The AST call-site-binding tests only inspect `execute_shard`; they cannot detect that the `mutmut run` in `_diagnose_non_killed` is unwrapped, so the same 'deleting the control is invisible' gap the author fixed for execute_shard still exists for the diagnostic path.
scenarios: A future edit (or the current omission) leaves `_diagnose_non_killed` unsandboxed and every test stays green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Log (at least at debug/warning) when a bwrap allow-list path is skipped for not existing, so a dropped writable bind is not silent.
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:169-172: `# bwrap's --bind requires SRC to exist ...\n        if not resolved.exists():\n            continue`
The gate mitigates this by `basetemp.mkdir(...)` before wrapping (scripts/mutation_gate.py:593), but the sandbox module itself gives no signal when an allow path is dropped.
advisory.finding: bwrap's missing-allow-path handling silently skips a writable bind (`continue`) rather than surfacing it; a nonexistent required path (e.g. basetemp not yet created by a future caller) becomes an invisible loss of the writable bind, indistinguishable from the path simply not being requested.
scenarios: A caller passes an allow path that does not yet exist; the writable bind is silently omitted and in-allow-list writes then fail (or, on the seatbelt path, behave differently), with no diagnostic.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct docs/local-dev-env.md so the sandbox allow-list description matches execute_shard's `sandbox_allow = (root, basetemp)` and removes the false 'and the venv' claim.
evidence: docs/local-dev-env.md:131-132: 'inside an OS sandbox that denies filesystem writes outside the scratch tree, the pytest basetemp, and the venv.'
scripts/mutation_gate.py:596: `sandbox_allow = (root, basetemp)` — the allow-list contains only root and basetemp, not the venv.
scripts/mutation_gate.py:594-595 (comment): 'sys.prefix is deliberately absent: a writable venv would let a mutant drop executable code into site-packages that later un-sandboxed phases import.'
scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:220-231: sandbox_env only sets HOME and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and adds no venv binding, so the venv is not writable.
advisory.finding: docs/local-dev-env.md describes the mutation-testing sandbox as permitting writes to 'the venv', but the code introduced in the same change deliberately excludes the venv from the allow-list so a mutant cannot write executable code into site-packages.
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/local-dev-env.md:131-132, replace 'the scratch tree, the pytest basetemp, and the venv' with the actual allow-list (the shard scratch tree and the pytest basetemp), and note that the venv is deliberately kept read-only per scripts/mutation_gate.py:594-595.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the sandbox denial tests with a producer-liveness assertion (e.g. assert the child ran to completion / an allowed sentinel write inside the same invocation succeeded) before trusting the absence check.
evidence: test_mutation_sandbox.py:78-79: `proc = subprocess.run(argv, ...); assert not target.exists(), f"sandbox permitted a write outside the allow-list; {_why(proc)}"` — `proc.returncode` and stdout are used only for the failure message, never asserted
test_mutation_sandbox.py:107-108: `assert keep.exists()` after `rm -rf` — same absence-shaped oracle with no anchor that the shell actually executed
test_mutation_sandbox.py:118-120: `assert not target.exists()` for the mutmut-run-shaped child, again with no producer-liveness assertion

If `sandbox-exec -f <profile>` rejects the generated profile, or the child never reaches the `echo`/`rm` for any reason, the target file is never created and the assertion passes — indistinguishable from a genuine deny. The companion positive test test_write_inside_the_allow_list_succeeds is a SEPARATE test and does not anchor liveness within the denial tests.
advisory.finding: The sandbox denial enforcement tests assert on file ABSENCE derived from a subprocess with no liveness check that the child actually ran, so they pass green both when the sandbox correctly denies the write AND when the sandbox wrapper fails to launch the child at all (malformed Seatbelt profile, exec failure, bwrap namespace error).
advisory.suggested_fix: In each denial test, also drive a control write to an ALLOWED path in the same subprocess invocation (e.g. `sh -c 'echo ok > <allowed>/marker && echo pwned > <outside>'`) and assert the allowed marker exists — proving the child executed — before asserting the outside/protected file was denied.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify or remove the `_ci_environment()` CI-conditional unsandboxed fallback in mutation_sandbox.py (and its doc/tests): the ticket's fail-closed AC authorizes only REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED and rejects any silent unsandboxed fallback.
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:193-202: `if _ci_environment(env):` ... `return list(argv)` (proceeds unsandboxed on CI)
scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:105 `def _ci_environment(env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> bool:`
AC: 'With no sandbox mechanism available the run ABORTS non-zero with a message naming REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED.'
AC: 'REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED=1 waives the sandbox and logs at WARNING; a silent unsandboxed fallback is rejected.'
Ticket description: 'Without bwrap, Linux fails closed.'
docs/local-dev-env.md:142 'On a CI runner (CI set truthy) the run proceeds UNSANDBOXED with a WARNING' — doc drift for the same unauthorized behavior
tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:364 test_ci_runner_proceeds_unsandboxed_with_a_warning and siblings (379, 386) exist solely to exercise this out-of-scope CI-waiver path
AC: 'The Linux write-deny is proven on Linux ... the same three-probe enforcement test runs in the ubuntu-latest CI leg' — a CI auto-waive undercuts proving enforcement on that leg
advisory.finding: A CI-conditional unsandboxed fallback (`_ci_environment()`) was added: when no sandbox mechanism is available and `CI` is truthy, `wrap()` returns the command UNWRAPPED with only a WARNING instead of aborting. No acceptance criterion authorizes this second waiver, and it contradicts the ticket's fail-closed intent, which names ONLY `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED` and states 'a silent unsandboxed fallback is rejected' / 'Without bwrap, Linux fails closed.'
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the `_ci_environment` branch (and its dedicated tests + doc paragraph) so the only unsandboxed path remains REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED, per the AC; if a CI-runner-is-disposable waiver is genuinely wanted, split it into its own ticket since it changes this ticket's committed fail-closed contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the CI unsandboxed fail-open in mutation_sandbox.wrap() cannot be triggered on a developer workstation by an inherited/ambient CI env var (e.g. require an explicit, non-inheritable signal or confirm ephemerality before waiving the sandbox).
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:192-202 `if mechanism is None: if _ci_environment(env): logger.warning(... UNSANDBOXED ...); return list(argv)`

scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:121-122 `raw = (env if env is not None else os.environ).get("CI", "")` then `return raw.strip().lower() not in {"", "0", "false", "no"}` — any truthy CI value waives the control
execute_shard passes env=_command_env(root) which is `dict(os.environ)` (scripts/mutation_gate.py:564, 575, 597), so the real process CI value flows into the CI check unmodified

Reachability: a mutation-gate run on a workstation where CI is exported truthy (common in shells, dotfiles, or inherited from a parent CI-emulating tool) takes the unsandboxed path with only a WARNING, re-exposing the exact rm -rf destructive-write path the module documents (scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:5-9)
advisory.finding: The sandbox fail-open branch keys on the ambient CI environment variable, so a workstation with CI set truthy silently runs mutation tests UNSANDBOXED instead of aborting — the CI variable is inheritable/trivially set and is the sole gate distinguishing 'disposable runner' from 'developer workstation', the machine the abort path exists to protect.
scenarios: Developer workstation with `CI=true` exported in shell profile runs the gate; probe() finds no mechanism; the destructive-write guard is silently waived.
A local CI-emulation or task runner that sets CI is used interactively on a real machine holding user files.
